phases.name: Prepare governed ML data
phases.description: Establish reproducible source data, preprocessing, and shared features before choosing training or serving paths.

phases.name: Train, compare, and version candidates
phases.description: Keep custom training and AutoML as distinct candidate paths and store immutable model and evaluation artifacts behind promotion gates.

phases.name: Serve online and batch predictions
phases.description: Expose a low-latency API path, a separate batch path, production monitoring, and interpretable outputs.

phases.name: Connect the ML lifecycle
phases.description: Connect data, feature, training, registry, release, inference, and feedback paths without treating drift signals as automatic production approval.

phases.name: Validate quality and operating targets
phases.description: Define evaluation populations and benchmark model accuracy, tail latency, throughput, and retraining cost before making claims.

steps.title: Freeze the exact problem brief
steps.content:
Title: Design a Machine Learning Platform
Description: Design an ML platform that trains custom models, automates ML workflows, deploys models as APIs, and monitors model performance in production.
Requirements:
1. Train custom ML models
2. Use AutoML for quick prototypes
3. Deploy models as endpoints
4. Perform batch predictions
5. Monitor model performance
6. Version control for models
7. Implement CI/CD for ML
8. Explain model predictions
Constraints:
1. Inference latency under 100ms
2. Support 10k predictions per second
3. Model accuracy above 90%
4. Cost-effective training
5. Automated model retraining
Hints:
1. Vertex AI for unified ML platform
2. AutoML for automated training
3. Cloud Functions for preprocessing
4. BigQuery ML for SQL-based ML
5. Feature Store for feature management
6. Vertex Explainable AI for interpretability

steps.title: Start from versioned source datasets
steps.content: Use the hinted BigQuery role for queryable training and batch-scoring inputs. Define data snapshots, access controls, labels, retention, and leakage checks; the brief does not state a domain or dataset size.

component.label: BigQuery Training and Scoring Data
component.description: Governed analytical source for training and batch prediction inputs.

properties.purpose: Provide governed, queryable datasets for feature preparation, model training, evaluation, and batch scoring; snapshot and label policy must prevent leakage and preserve reproducibility.

component.highlightReason: Both training and batch predictions need an auditable data source; BigQuery ML is among the supplied hints.

steps.title: Validate and preprocess before feature computation
steps.content: Represent repeatable preprocessing and schema validation as a reusable stage. The hint names Cloud Functions, but the brief does not establish event volume or execution duration; choose serverless versus distributed execution from measured workload.

component.label: Preprocessing and Validation
component.description: Versioned transforms, input validation, and data-quality checks.

properties.purpose: Apply versioned preprocessing and schema/data-quality validation consistently to training and inference inputs; choose execution size and runtime from actual volume and duration.

component.highlightReason: Consistent preprocessing prevents training-serving skew and keeps data-quality behavior explicit.

steps.title: Share point-in-time-correct features
steps.content: Use the hinted feature-store boundary for reusable feature definitions and online/offline consistency. Preserve point-in-time joins for training so evaluation does not leak future information; the platform choice and feature count are unspecified.

component.label: Feature Store
component.description: Reusable offline and online feature definitions and values.

properties.purpose: Manage reusable feature definitions and aligned offline/online values; enforce point-in-time-correct training joins and consistent transformations without assuming feature volume or vendor.

component.highlightReason: Feature management is an explicit hint and reduces divergence between training and online inference.

steps.title: Train custom models as reproducible runs
steps.content: Record code revision, data snapshot, feature definitions, parameters, environment, and metrics for each custom training run. Select CPU/GPU/TPU and distributed mode only after profiling the model and cost envelope.

component.label: Custom Model Training
component.description: Reproducible training jobs for domain-specific models.

properties.purpose: Train custom candidate models from versioned data and features while recording source revision, parameters, environment, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility metadata; compute type follows profiling.

component.highlightReason: Custom model training is a core requirement and needs reproducible inputs to support safe evaluation and retraining.

steps.title: Keep AutoML as a rapid prototype path
steps.content: Use AutoML for quick baselines or prototypes when task/data support fits. Compare candidates on the same held-out, representative evaluation set; an AutoML result is not automatically suitable for production or guaranteed to exceed the accuracy target.

component.label: AutoML Prototype Models
component.description: Managed AutoML candidate path for rapid baseline experiments.

properties.purpose: Generate rapid candidate baselines when the task is supported; evaluate against the same held-out representative data and operational criteria as custom models before promotion.

component.highlightReason: AutoML is explicitly required for quick prototypes and is best treated as a candidate-generation path.

steps.title: Version model artifacts and their evidence
steps.content: Store immutable model artifacts alongside metadata that identifies source code, data snapshot, feature definitions, evaluation report, and approval state. Cloud Storage can hold artifact bytes, but the brief does not specify a registry product or retention policy.

component.label: Versioned Model and Evaluation Artifacts
component.description: Immutable storage for model packages and linked provenance/evaluation records.

properties.purpose: Retain immutable model packages and linked data/code/feature provenance, evaluation reports, and approval metadata so deployed and rollback versions are identifiable.

component.highlightReason: Model version control is an explicit requirement and must include the artifact plus the evidence needed to reproduce its evaluation.

steps.title: Promote models through an ML CI/CD gate
steps.content: Automate tests, data/model validation, artifact checks, staged deployment, and rollback. A new candidate should not replace production merely because training completed or drift was detected; require an explicit quality and safety gate.

component.label: ML Build, Evaluation, and Release Pipeline
component.description: Versioned tests and gated promotion for data, model, and serving changes.

properties.componentName: ML Build, Evaluation, and Release Pipeline
properties.purpose: Test preprocessing and serving contracts, evaluate candidate artifacts, verify provenance, and promote through staged deployment with rollback; production approval remains gated on quality and operational checks.

component.highlightReason: ML CI/CD is explicit; separating model creation from controlled deployment avoids unsafe automatic promotion.

steps.title: Define model-quality and retraining policy
steps.content: The 90% accuracy target is not meaningful until the metric, class balance, evaluation slice, confidence interval, and data representativeness are specified. Automated retraining can create candidates on schedule or drift triggers; promotion should still require validation and a controlled release decision.

steps.title: Expose a stable authenticated inference API
steps.content: Put request validation, authentication, quotas, and API versioning in front of online inference. Define payload size, timeout, error behavior, and latency measurement boundary; the brief does not provide a percentile for the 100ms limit.

component.label: Online Prediction API
component.description: Versioned request boundary for real-time model predictions.

properties.purpose: Validate and authenticate versioned prediction requests, enforce bounded request behavior, and route to the currently approved endpoint; define payload, timeout, and latency measurement contract.

component.highlightReason: Deploying models as endpoints requires a controlled API boundary, and the 100ms target must be measured from a defined request edge.

steps.title: Serve only the approved model version
steps.content: Run the selected model behind a managed endpoint with readiness checks, bounded concurrency, and rollback to a known version. Estimate replica capacity and accelerator choice through load tests instead of deriving it solely from the 10k/s target.

component.label: Approved Online Model Endpoint
component.description: Low-latency inference for the currently promoted model version.

properties.purpose: Serve only a promoted immutable model version behind readiness and health checks; size concurrency, replicas, and accelerators from representative load tests and cost constraints.

component.highlightReason: The API endpoint and 10k predictions/second requirement make serving capacity and model version explicit.

steps.title: Keep bulk scoring off the synchronous request path
steps.content: Use a separate batch-scoring worker to read a bounded dataset, invoke a selected model artifact, and write results with job and source identifiers. This isolates large jobs from interactive endpoint capacity and makes retries auditable.

component.label: Batch Prediction Worker
component.description: Asynchronous scoring jobs over warehouse datasets.

properties.purpose: Run asynchronous, restartable scoring jobs over identified warehouse inputs and write outputs with job/model version provenance; keep bulk work isolated from online endpoint capacity.

component.highlightReason: Batch predictions are a separate requirement and should not consume the interactive latency budget.

steps.title: Watch service and model quality in production
steps.content: Monitor request latency and errors alongside model-quality slices, input feature distribution, drift, batch job success, and prediction volumes. Choose labels and ground-truth delay expectations with the domain; not all predictions can be scored immediately.

component.label: Model and Serving Monitoring
component.description: Operational and delayed quality/drift signals for online and batch models.

properties.purpose: Track endpoint latency/errors/throughput, batch job health, feature distributions, drift indicators, and delayed labeled quality slices to initiate investigation or a candidate retraining run.

component.highlightReason: Model performance monitoring and automated retraining both depend on observable operational and quality signals.

steps.title: Return useful explanations with model outputs
steps.content: Add an explanation capability appropriate to the model family and explanation method, such as the hinted Vertex Explainable AI. Explanations should state the method and limitations; do not present feature attribution as causal proof.

component.label: Prediction Explanation Service
component.description: Produces model-appropriate attribution or explanation metadata.

properties.purpose: Generate model-appropriate explanation metadata for prediction responses and identify the explanation method and limitations; do not imply attribution establishes causality.

component.highlightReason: Explainability is a functional requirement and needs an explicit response path, not only an offline model note.

steps.title: Apply consistent transforms to source data
steps.content: Versioned source snapshots feed validation and preprocessing so model runs can reproduce the same feature inputs.

connection.label: snapshot and validate source data
connection.description: BigQuery snapshots provide identified data for shared preprocessing and quality checks.

steps.title: Materialize consistent offline and online features
steps.content: Preprocessing writes governed feature values and definitions to the feature-store boundary so training and serving can share transformations.

connection.label: validated feature values
connection.description: Versioned transforms populate shared offline/online feature definitions and values.

steps.title: Train custom candidates from point-in-time features
steps.content: Custom training reads aligned feature snapshots and records their version with each run, avoiding train/serve skew and data leakage.

connection.label: versioned offline features
connection.description: Custom training consumes point-in-time-correct features and preserves their version in run provenance.

steps.title: Feed AutoML from the same evaluation-ready inputs
steps.content: Use consistent feature and evaluation splits for the AutoML prototype path so baseline comparisons are fair and reproducible.

connection.label: shared candidate inputs
connection.description: AutoML prototypes consume governed features and comparable evaluation splits.

steps.title: Persist custom model packages and evaluation evidence
steps.content: Store the produced package, run metadata, and evaluation report together with immutable identifiers so a deployment maps back to exact training inputs.

connection.label: custom model and provenance
connection.description: Custom training publishes immutable package and provenance/evaluation metadata to versioned storage.

steps.title: Version AutoML candidates using the same contract
steps.content: Store AutoML artifacts and comparable quality reports under the same provenance and review contract as custom candidates.

connection.label: AutoML model and evaluation
connection.description: AutoML candidates are versioned with their evaluation evidence before consideration for promotion.

steps.title: Release only a verified immutable candidate
steps.content: The release pipeline retrieves a specific artifact and verifies provenance, test results, model-quality criteria, and approval metadata before deployment.

connection.label: verified model package
connection.description: CI/CD consumes an immutable candidate and its quality/provenance evidence for gated rollout.

steps.title: Deploy through staged endpoint promotion
steps.content: Promote a candidate to the serving endpoint only after checks pass, and retain a known-good version for rollback if health or quality regresses.

connection.label: approved model version
connection.description: The release pipeline deploys a checked immutable version and supports controlled rollback.

steps.title: Route validated online requests to inference
steps.content: The API gateway sends bounded, authenticated requests to the approved endpoint; measure full client-to-response latency at a defined percentile, including feature lookup and explanation cost.

connection.label: validated prediction request
connection.description: Online API requests are routed to the approved model endpoint with bounded request behavior.

steps.title: Fetch online features within the latency budget
steps.content: The endpoint retrieves only features needed for prediction from the online store and returns a controlled error or fallback if required features are unavailable; include this dependency in tail-latency tests.

connection.label: low-latency feature values
connection.description: Inference uses current online feature values consistent with the trained feature definitions.

steps.title: Attach method-labeled explanations to predictions
steps.content: Where explanation is part of the response contract, obtain attribution metadata from the model-appropriate explanation service and document the additional latency and limitations.

connection.label: prediction attribution
connection.description: The serving path requests model-appropriate explanation metadata for the prediction response.

steps.title: Select identified warehouse rows for batch jobs
steps.content: Batch jobs select a stable input snapshot, persist job identity and model version, and can resume or retry without confusing partial outputs with completion.

connection.label: identified scoring dataset
connection.description: The batch worker reads a stable BigQuery input snapshot and tracks job/model identity.

steps.title: Run batch scoring against an explicit model version
steps.content: Load an explicitly selected immutable artifact so a retry or rerun can reproduce which model generated each result.

connection.label: versioned scoring model
connection.description: Batch scoring resolves a fixed artifact version with provenance rather than implicitly using the latest model.

steps.title: Persist batch outputs with lineage
steps.content: Write prediction results with the source snapshot, model version, and job identity so downstream consumers can distinguish complete outputs from retries or partial runs.

connection.label: lineaged batch results
connection.description: Batch predictions are persisted for analysis with explicit input and model lineage.

steps.title: Measure production quality and serving health
steps.content: Collect tail latency, throughput, errors, resource saturation, feature drift, and delayed quality labels; compare slices against the agreed accuracy definition.

connection.label: latency, volume, and model signals
connection.description: Online model service and delayed quality signals feed production monitoring.

steps.title: Observe batch completion and prediction quality
steps.content: Track batch job completion, row counts, retries, prediction distributions, and label-based quality when feedback arrives.

connection.label: job and output health
connection.description: Batch scoring health and result quality are monitored independently from online serving.

steps.title: Trigger retraining candidates without bypassing promotion
steps.content: Drift or scheduled policy can initiate a new evaluation/training run through CI/CD, but an alert is not proof that new data is valid or a new model is better. Retain validation and staged promotion gates.

connection.label: scheduled or drift-triggered candidate run
connection.description: Monitoring can initiate an automated retraining workflow while preserving evaluation and production-promotion gates.

steps.title: Let the pipeline orchestrate reproducible retraining
steps.content: The release/orchestration workflow starts a new custom training run using approved data and code revisions, then sends its result through the same artifact and evaluation checks. This closes the automated retraining loop without granting the trigger direct production access.

connection.label: start versioned candidate run
connection.description: The orchestrator launches reproducible training from approved inputs and returns candidates to the normal evaluation and promotion path.

steps.title: Benchmark on representative traffic and evaluation slices
steps.content: The brief omits model task, accuracy metric, input size, percentile for 100ms, regional scope, prediction mix, data-label delay, retraining cadence, and cost budget. Benchmark end-to-end requests—including feature lookup and explanations—at 10k/s, measure quality on representative held-out and monitored slices, and verify retraining produces candidates that still pass the same release gates.
